finalText:
Redis crashed at 02:14:07 (connection refused to 10.0.0.12:6379), and your app didn't survive losing it.

Without caching, every request hit the database directly. The store couldn't keep up — requests timed out after 5 seconds, and new ones piled into the queue faster than they drained. Queue depth climbed past your 500-item limit, hitting 562–568 by 02:31.

The backlog consumed memory steadily. At 02:31:44, a worker process exhausted the JavaScript heap and crashed. A minute later, the API was unresponsive, so the supervisor killed everything.

**The core issue:** When Redis went down, there was no circuit breaker or load shedding to keep the store from drowning. Every incoming request tried the database, amplifying the problem.

Quick wins: (1) Add a cache circuit breaker that returns an error or cached stale data if Redis is down, instead of hammering the store. (2) Implement request queue backpressure — once the queue hits a threshold, reject new requests rather than letting it grow. (3) Monitor Redis health separately so you catch the outage before the cascade.

Redis also never reconnected during those 17 minutes of retries — worth checking if the Redis instance is actually back, or if the network route is still broken.
